maya: Quick design drop — compact chat toolbar iteration. Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/abcd/playground-compact-toolbar (look at frames 3–6). thoughts on streaming tokens vs simple 'typing' indicator? jo: Love the compact toolbar. Main worry: streaming token jitter will make layout jump on low-width screens. can we keep height stable? :eyes: priya: Agree on stable height. Maybe render tokens into an overflow area that animates opacity instead of changing layout. also need keyboard focus state for stop/regenerate buttons. alex: For streaming specifically, can we show progressive text but only update token counter every 250ms? That smooths updates and reduces reflow. Also we should debounce the token meter when network hiccups occur. maya: Good call on debounce. What about button order — current is [Stop] [Regenerate]. Some folks expect Regenerate on right. UX opinion? ben: I'd prefer Stop on left (primary action while generation active) and Regenerate tucked to the right. But label change: 'Stop' -> 'Stop generation' for a11y clarity? screen readers get 'Stop' ambiguous. priya: Yes long labels help. Also for screen readers we should expose generation state with `aria-live` and a succinct message. Example: `aria-live=\"polite\"` with "Generation in progress" then "Generation completed". alex: Quick code snippet for the live region we prototyped earlier: ```
Generation in progress
``` This plus visually-hidden text on state transitions should be fine. sam: Token counter placement question: inline next to timestamp vs a small pill on the far right? On narrow widths inline steals space from content. I vote pill. maya: Pill seems to be the consensus. Should it show estimated tokens while streaming and final count on completion? jo: Yes — show an estimated live count with a subtle `~` prefix (e.g., `~120`) and remove tilde once final. Also add tooltip explaining estimate vs exact. ben: Can we also offer a memory-saver mode in settings that hides live token updates entirely? For low-end devices, polling the model for token stats is expensive. priya: Good feature. Settings toggle: "Show live token meter" default on. Remember to persist per-account and per-playground workspace. maya: Prompt library integration: suggestion to add quick-insert icon inside toolbar (small plus) that opens the docked prompt drawer. Thoughts on discoverability? alex: Quick-insert icon is fine but needs a11y label and keyboard shortcut. Recommend `Ctrl+K` opens prompt drawer and focus lands on search. priya: Also need ARIA role for the drawer: `role=\"dialog\" aria-modal=\"true\"` when docked? If it's a persistent dock maybe just `role=\"complementary\"` and ensure keyboard trapping only for modal. sam: On mobile the drawer should slide up from bottom not dock right. We need a breakpoint behavior doc. maya: Adding mobile breakpoint behavior to the figma comments. Also attaching a short prototype showing focus outlines and contrast. ago: (typo) meant alex* — ignore jo: Minor copy tweak: change "Regenerate" tooltip to "Regenerate response (preserves chat history)" — clarifies behavior. ben: Accessibility nit: stop button contrast at 32px needs to meet 4.5:1. Current red variant is borderline. priya: I'll run the color through Axe and post results. qa-bot: automated test note — add e2e tests for keyboard flows: open prompt drawer, insert prompt, start generation, stop with keyboard, regenerate with keyboard. I'll add to the test plan. maya: Thanks — next steps: Priya to run contrast checks and implement aria-live region; Alex to add debounce and batch token updates; Jo to update copy; Ben to provide alt colors; Sam to write responsive breakpoint rules; QA to add tests. I'll do a canary UI rollout for 10% initially. jo: +1 on canary. Also add telemetry events: `playground.generation_started`, `.stopped`, `.regenerated`, `.token_meter_shown` (with boolean for estimated). alex: For telemetry, include `device_width` so we can gauge mobile impact. priya: I'll post follow-up with accessibility test results and an a11y checklist. maya: Sweet — thanks everyone. If you have micro-ux nits, drop them as figma comments or inline here. :thumbsup:
